newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end firmer, buoyed by shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end firmer, buoyed by shortcovering.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in thin trade on Monday, buoyed by strength in U.S. Treasuries and further covering of short positions following Friday's rally, analysts said.

"I think there's some residual shorts left from Friday," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research at Midland Walwyn Capital. "I don't think anyone is overly bullish right now. We have some pretty big numbers coming out this week."
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 rose C$0.58 to C$101.33 to yield 7.878 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 14/32 to yield 7.07 percent.
The spread between benchmark bonds narrowed to 81 basis points from 83 basis points at Friday's close.

Canadian and U.S. bond markets strengthened on Friday in a short-covering rally prompted by the release of U.S. non-farm payrolls data. Prices rose further today as traders continued to cover shorts amid a lack of economic data, analysts said.

"I think it's just a followthrough now that the payrolls are behind us and there's just a little short-covering here. I don't think anything has really changed," said Will Sutherland, vice-president of fixed-income for Altamira Investment Services.
Investors are now looking ahead to release of key economic data later this week, including U.S. producer price data on Thursday and Canadian and U.S. consumer price data on Friday, analysts said.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.60 to C$97.12 to yield 7.405 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 10/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 53 basis points from 57 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.98 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.28 percent.
